open_points.subject: Project revision on archive and anonymise
open_points.text: A Project and a Customer carry a revision, an ordinal starting at 1 that every accepted change moves by one.
open_points.question: Does archiving a project (and anonymising it) count as an accepted change that moves the project's revision, and must the archive action state the revision it was made against (stale refused) like a correction?
options: archiving moves the revision and states one
archiving moves the revision but states none
archiving moves neither; only corrections touch the revision
open_points.default_guess: archiving moves the revision by one and must state the revision it was made against; anonymising does not (the revision goes with the card)

open_points.subject: Customer revision and the marks
open_points.text: A Customer's last-changed instant moves by: a correction of its contact, kind or fiscal data; restricting and lifting; ending and resuming the relationship; erasure.
open_points.question: Do restricting, lifting, ending, resuming and erasing move the Customer's revision, and must those actions state the revision they were made against?
options: every mark change moves the revision and states one
mark changes move the revision but state none
only corrections move the revision
open_points.default_guess: every accepted change of a Customer, marks included, moves the revision and must state the one it was made against

open_points.subject: Last-changed instant: written once vs moving
open_points.text: Written once, derived and not a fact of its own: the last-changed instant
open_points.question: Is the project's last-changed instant a stored fact that moves with each correction and with archiving (as 'Revisions and times' says), or derived — and if derived, from what, given Registry keeps no change history and the audit log may be erased by date?
options: a stored fact of the Project, overwritten on each qualifying change
derived from the audit log
derived from the revision's own instant
open_points.default_guess: a stored fact of the Project, overwritten by each change 'Revisions and times' names; 'written once, derived' is a slip

open_points.subject: Imported records' instants and revisions
open_points.text: A record carries the instant it was created and the instant it was last changed;
open_points.question: For projects, customers, rooms and pointers the import brings in, are the created and last-changed instants, the archived instant and the revision kept from the v1 export or set at the import (revision 1, created = import instant)?
options: kept from v1 where v1 has them, otherwise set at import
always set at import
kept from v1 for instants, revision restarts at 1
open_points.default_guess: created and archived instants kept from v1 where present; last-changed instant and revision set at import (revision 1)

open_points.subject: What an erased Customer keeps
open_points.text: the Customer keeps only its identity and the fact that it was erased; name, phone, e-mail and language are gone; projects still name it (R0-06)
open_points.question: State 0 says an erased Customer keeps its identity and the erased mark and nothing else; State 1 M04 keeps its kind and the restricted and ended marks (with their dates and instants) as well. Which is it, and if State 1's answer stands, which State 0 decision records the change (R0-75)?
options: identity and erased mark only, as State 0 says
identity, kind and erased mark, marks cleared
identity, kind, erased mark and the other marks, as State 1 says — new owner decision in State 0
open_points.default_guess: State 1's list stands and State 0 gains a decision narrowing R0-06/R0-67 to say kind and marks survive

open_points.subject: Erasure of fiscal data
open_points.text: Erasing a customer's contact data (R0-06) is the end of its record
open_points.question: State 0's action is 'erase a customer's contact data' and lists name, phone, e-mail and language as gone; State 1 M04 also erases tax id and legal name. Does the one erase action remove fiscal data too, or is fiscal data erased separately (or never)?
options: one erasure removes contact and fiscal data together
contact data and fiscal data are erased by separate actions
fiscal data is never erased by Registry
open_points.default_guess: one erasure removes contact and fiscal data together, and State 0's action text is widened to say so

open_points.subject: Marks after erasure and the erased read
open_points.text: The three marks stay independent facts; erasure clears none of them.
open_points.question: The lifecycle says what erasure does to the other marks 'is settled in State 2 if anything', the Open questions say it is settled (clears none), and the erased read shows 'no other value' than ref, kind and erased mark. Are the restricted and ended marks kept after erasure, and if kept, are they shown in the read and list of an erased Customer?
options: kept and shown
kept but not shown
cleared by erasure
open_points.default_guess: kept as facts and shown in the owner's read and list (they carry no personal value); the lifecycle sentence is a slip

open_points.subject: Kind and name of the import-made Customer
open_points.text: The Customer the import makes from a v1 `customer_ref` (R0-80) gets its tax id from the v1 value when it is one and an absent name; the owner gives the name after the import, as the import gives display names (R0-85).
open_points.question: What kind (person or company) does the Customer the import makes get, given 'record a customer' refuses a missing kind, and is its name given in the import itself (as R0-85 does for display names) or afterwards by a correction?
options: the owner gives kind and name in the import, per customer
kind derived from the tax id form, name given afterwards
kind absent until corrected
open_points.default_guess: the owner gives kind and name per Customer in the import, as for project names; nothing is derived from the tax id

open_points.subject: Source of imported Customer facts; one Customer per v1 value
open_points.text: its identity `customer_ref`, minted by Registry (R0-16) or kept by the import when it is a Registry-minted one (R0-80);
open_points.question: When a v1 `customer_ref` is a Registry-minted id, where do the Customer's contact and fiscal facts come from — does the v1 export carry Customer records? And when several imported projects share one non-minted v1 value, does the import make one Customer or one per project?
options: the export carries v1 Customer records; one Customer per distinct v1 value
no v1 Customer records; every imported Customer starts with only what the owner gives in the import; one per distinct value
one Customer per project
open_points.default_guess: one Customer per distinct v1 value; its facts come from the v1 Customer record when the export has one, otherwise from the owner in the import

open_points.subject: Identity format left open vs ids kept
open_points.text: the owner may choose otherwise, and the import then maps v1 ids, which it today keeps verbatim.
open_points.question: Is the UUID format settled? R0-50, R0-79 and R0-85 say the import keeps ids verbatim ('under the ids Client Portal already names'); a mapping would break them. Which holds?
options: UUID is settled; the escape clause is removed
another format with a mapping, and State 0's 'ids kept' is reopened
open_points.default_guess: UUID is settled and the import keeps every id verbatim

open_points.subject: Identities not in the minted list
open_points.text: Every identity Registry mints — `project_id`, `room_id`, artifact pointer id, `customer_ref` — is an opaque identifier with no meaning in its form.
open_points.question: The OwnerSession id (M11, 'minted by Registry at sign-in') and the confirmation id (M09, M10) are also minted by Registry but are absent from this list. Do they fall under the same rule (opaque, UUID), and is either ever written into a durable record?
options: same rule; the confirmation id is durable in audit entries and the closure, the session id never
the owner session id and confirmation id are State 2 mechanisms, not identities
open_points.default_guess: same opaque rule; the confirmation id is durable in audit entries and the migration closure, the owner session id is runtime only

open_points.subject: Confirmation id: what it identifies
open_points.text: the confirmation id where the owner confirmed (R0-37);
open_points.question: What is a confirmation id — the identity of a confirmation step the owner interface minted, of the owner session, or of the confirmed request — who mints it, and is there a Confirmation model (none is listed among M01–M11) or is it a value with no record of its own?
options: an id Registry mints when the owner confirms, recorded only in the audit entry and the closure
the owner session id
a value of the owner interface's form, stored as given
open_points.default_guess: an opaque id Registry mints per confirmed action, with no model of its own, recorded only where R0-37 names it

open_points.subject: Which actions write an entry
open_points.text: the change: which action, in a closed vocabulary State 6 declares;
open_points.question: R0-58 names changes to projects and customer records, grants and revocations, restriction, erasures. Do creating a project or recording a customer, adding a room, publishing or withdrawing a pointer, changing or clearing the active project, declining a request, registering a session, and the import itself each write an entry?
options: every owner write and the import write one; room adds and pointer publishes do not
every write of any principal writes one
only the actions R0-58 lists verbatim
open_points.default_guess: create, record, correct, archive, erase, anonymise, grant, revoke, active-project change, decline, restrict/lift, end/resume, import and audit erasure write one; room adds, pointer publishes/withdrawals and session registrations do not

open_points.subject: Subject of entries without one project or customer
open_points.text: the subject: the project (`project_id`) or the customer (`customer_ref`) changed, by identity only (R0-37) — for a session grant, the session and the project;
open_points.question: What is the subject of the import's entry (several projects and customers), of the erasure of old entries, of an active-project change or a declined request (a session alone), and of a change to the Customer that a project links to?
options: the import's subject is the closure's file digest; session changes name the session alone; the audit erasure has none
one entry per imported project and customer
subject optional
open_points.default_guess: the import's entry names the file digest and the ids imported; session-only changes name the session; the audit erasure names only its date

open_points.subject: Access version: settled or deferred
open_points.text: its access version, an ordinal that every change of the granted set, the active project or the pending request moves (R0-64; round 28 P4 — the precise semantics are State 2's);
open_points.question: The facts say every change of the set, the active project or the pending request moves the version; the Open questions say what moves it is State 2's. Is the list of movers settled here (so a new or replaced request moves it), and does a pending request's replacement by an equal text move it?
options: settled here as written; State 2 fixes only the start value
entirely State 2's; the facts sentence is a candidate
open_points.default_guess: settled as written: set, active project and pending request changes each move it; the start is State 2's

open_points.subject: What an anonymised project keeps
open_points.text: An anonymised project keeps its id, status and artifact pointers and nothing else.
open_points.question: State 0 (R0-62, R0-60) keeps id, status and pointers and nothing else; State 1 M01 also keeps the archived instant and the anonymised instant (settled by the owner on 2026-10-31). Which stands, and where is the State 0 change recorded (R0-75 makes it a new owner decision there)?
options: State 1's list stands; State 0 gains a decision narrowing R0-62
State 0 stands; the instants go too
open_points.default_guess: State 1's list stands and State 0 records it as a decision narrowing R0-60/R0-62

open_points.subject: Anonymised project: lifecycle text vs facts
open_points.text: it keeps its `project_id`, its status, its archived instant and its artifact pointers (M05) and nothing else — name, alias, object, customer link, rooms and revision are gone (R0-62; see Open questions).
open_points.question: The lifecycle omits the anonymised instant that the facts and the settled Open questions keep, and points to Open questions that read 'None'. Does an anonymised project keep the anonymised instant, and is the created instant kept or gone?
options: keeps archived and anonymised instants, created instant gone
keeps created, archived and anonymised instants
keeps archived instant only
open_points.default_guess: keeps the archived and anonymised instants; the created instant goes with the card

open_points.subject: Display name uniqueness
open_points.text: its display name, given by the owner, naming the object and the work and never a person (R0-82), held as `personal_data`;
open_points.question: May two projects carry the same display name (the alias is settled as non-unique, the name is not addressed), and does Registry refuse a duplicate on create or correct?
options: no uniqueness; duplicates allowed
unique among active projects
unique among all projects
open_points.default_guess: no uniqueness rule; Registry refuses no duplicate name, as it merges nothing that looks alike (R0-34)

open_points.subject: Object kind as a vocabulary
open_points.text: Facts: address (required); kind; the declared characteristics (their list is the specification's and belongs to State 6).
open_points.question: Is the object's kind a closed set the specification declares (then it belongs under 'Declared vocabularies', which does not list it) or free text the owner writes? The same question holds for the Customer's language.
options: closed vocabulary declared in State 6, listed under Declared vocabularies
free text, personal_data, as written by the owner
open_points.default_guess: object kind is a closed vocabulary declared in State 6 and added to Declared vocabularies; language is free text

open_points.subject: Principal as a fact of the Room
open_points.text: written once: the instant it was added and by which principal (M07) — the owner or the agent through Kernel naming its session
open_points.question: State 0's 'add a room' output names id, name and project only, and R0-58 says agent calls are not recorded. Is the adding principal (with the agent's session identity) a fact of the Room that 'list rooms' exposes to every reader — Kernel for another session included — or an internal fact no answer carries?
options: a fact of the Room, exposed in reads
a fact of the Room, never exposed
not a fact of the Room
open_points.default_guess: a stored fact of the Room, carried in the owner's reads and not in the agent projection or Kernel's list
